implementation_notes: TypeScript makes the field-shaped scatter a compile error, which is the single biggest reason it is cheaper here than in JavaScript: adding a required property to an interface names every producer that must change. The residual scatter comes from types that are re-declared rather than imported, and from `Partial<T>` / index signatures that erase the requirement. The idiomatic fix is to import the one interface everywhere and derive the transport shape with `Omit`/`Pick` rather than re-declaring it.
idiom_name: optional field added to every interface that describes the shape
pitfalls: `Partial<T>` on the wire type removes the exhaustiveness check that would have caught a missing producer.
An index signature `[k: string]: any` on a DTO makes any shape assignment legal, so the scatter cannot be caught.
`Omit` chains can hide a required field from the compiler while it is still required at runtime.
